summary: Upstream throws a catchable Error on cyclic (non-DAG) sankey input; the Swift port maps it to fatalError(), which crashes the entire host process on invalid user data instead of surfacing a recoverable error.

summary: logBase read via `as? Double` silently returns nil for an Int-literal option (logBase: 2), dropping the user value — the known Int-vs-Double option-read trap.
evidence: CONFIRMED real bug — the documented Int-vs-Double option-read trap. `model.get("logBase") as? Double` returns nil for an Int-literal `logBase: 2`. That nil flows to LogScaleSetting.logBase, and LogScale.swift:112 `self.base = number.or(setting.logBase, 10)` then silently defaults base to 10. A user's `logBase: 2` is dropped -> wrong log-axis scaling. Matches the memory'd critical-class trap; needs an Int/Double coercion helper.

summary: Concrete `getArea(_:)->Cartesian2DArea` does not witness protocol `getArea()->CoordinateSystemClipArea?` and — unlike getAxis/getOtherAxis — got NO Phase-51 delegating overload, so callers using a CoordinateSystem existential (e.g. MarkPointView.swift:54, createClipPathFromCoordSys.swift:260) hit the nil-returning default and lose the clip area.
evidence: Empirically compiled a minimal swiftc repro (protocol getArea(_:)->ClipArea? + default nil; concrete getArea(_ :Double?=nil)->ConformingStruct): the concrete does NOT witness the optional-existential requirement -> DEFAULT (nil) runs through the existential. No delegating overload exists for getArea (unlike getAxis/getOtherAxis at 259-266). Both callers use the CoordinateSystem existential: MarkPointView.swift:54 `coordSys = ...as? CoordinateSystem; coordSys?.getArea(nil)` -> nil (markPoint relativeTo:coordinate loses width/height/x/y), and createClipPathFromCoordSys.swift:260 `coordSys.getArea(0.1)` -> nil (scatter/line symbol clipping silently disabled).

summary: Value-semantics workaround writes index-prepended data back to self.option['data']; unlike upstream's dual-alias trick, a later mergeOption that does not replace data would double-prepend the base-category index.

summary: Piecewise selected flag looked up by best-effort index-string key instead of PiecewiseModel.getSelectedMapKey (which is ported), so geo heatmap piece selection can mis-map vs upstream.

summary: designatedVisualItemStyle is a value-type dict, so treemapVisual's in-place write-through into the live-shared object is lost — and treemapVisual.swift is now ported, making this an active visual-priority bug, not a future concern.

Parent-designated colorAlpha/colorSaturation inheritance does not take effect.

summary: Upstream's `dimItem && ...` guard is dropped on the claim that idx always indexes an existing dim, but SeriesData.getDimensionInfo force-unwraps (_getDimInfo(...)!) so a data row whose value array is longer than the declared dimensions makes getDimensionInfo(idx) return nil and SIGTRAPs.
evidence: Confirmed as a latent crash, though the crash mechanism differs slightly from the claim. Loop at line 122 iterates idx in 0..<value.count (value = series.getRawValue, the raw user row) calling getDimensionInfo(idx). getDimensionInfo (SeriesData.swift:476-481) force-unwraps _getDimInfo(...)!, and getDimension (line 398-399) does self.dimensions[Int(dimIdx!)] with dimIdx = idx unchanged (_recognizeDimIndex returns the number as-is for numeric input, line 451-452). So a data row LONGER than declared dimensions crashes — either an out-of-bounds on dimensions[idx] (non-omitted case) or the '!' nil unwrap — matching why upstream keeps the 'dimItem && ...' guard that the port dropped. Reachability requires an over-long row (uncommon since dimension inference usually sizes dims to the data), so medium rather than high.

summary: Force-unwrap of getDataDimensionIndex(data)! traps if the dimension resolves to nil (upstream tolerates undefined).
evidence: data.each(self.getDataDimensionIndex(data)!) force-unwraps an Optional DimensionIndex inside findTargetDataIndices (hoverLink/selection targeting). Upstream JS tolerates undefined (data.each(undefined,...) iterates default dim). If the visualMap dimension fails to resolve against a target series' data, this SIGTRAPs. Live path (hoverLink), but only on an unresolved-dimension edge -> medium.

summary: CoordinateSystemMaster optional methods (getRect/getAxes/getTooltipAxes/convert*) given silent nil/no-op defaults; a conformer whose concrete method has a narrower signature fails to witness and silently hits the nil default (the documented protocol-witness trap, e.g. getRect).
evidence: Confirmed: extension (152-169) gives nil/no-op defaults to every optional CoordinateSystemMaster method (getRect/getAxes/getTooltipAxes/convert*). This is exactly the documented protocol-witness trap — a conformer whose concrete method has a narrower (e.g. non-optional-return) signature fails to witness and silently dispatches the nil default. Real latent risk; live sites work around it by concrete-type casts.

summary: CoordinateSystem optional methods (getBaseAxis/getAxis/getRect/getViewRect/etc.) given nil-returning defaults; a concrete non-optional-return witness (e.g. Cartesian2D.getBaseAxis/getAxis) silently fails to witness and dispatches the nil default — the exact trap Series.swift getBaseAxis/indicesOfNearest work around by casting to Cartesian2D.
evidence: Confirmed: extension (309-326) nil-defaults getBaseAxis/getAxis/getRect/getViewRect/etc. Matches the memory-documented trap that Series.swift getBaseAxis/indicesOfNearest already work around by casting to Cartesian2D. A concrete non-optional-return witness silently fails to satisfy and hits the nil default → wrong axis/geometry. Genuine standing risk.

summary: Non-string, non-collect branch returns `(category as? Double) ?? NaN`; an OrdinalNumber index arriving boxed as Int fails the Double cast and silently becomes NaN (the known Int-vs-Double option-read trap).
evidence: Actual code L128: `return (category as? OrdinalNumber) ?? OrdinalNumber.nan`; OrdinalNumber = Double (types.swift:625), so this IS `(category as? Double) ?? NaN`. Sole live caller is DataStore.swift:328 `ordinalMeta.parseAndCollect(self._chunks[dimIdx][i])`; _chunks is [[ParsedValue]] and ParsedValue = Any (types.swift:640), populated from raw source parse (defaultDimValueGetters), so it CAN box an Int. Branch fires when !isString && !needCollect (axis with predefined categories, numeric index case). An Int-boxed index fails `as? Double` -> NaN -> datum silently dropped. Matches the documented Int-vs-Double trap. Reachability is narrow (predefined-category axis fed numeric indices) hence medium not high.

summary: getDimensionInfo force-unwraps _getDimInfo(...)!; a caller passing a dim absent from _dimInfos traps instead of getting undefined as upstream.
evidence: Confirmed force-unwrap `self._getDimInfo(...)!` at line 480. Upstream returns undefined; here a dim absent from _dimInfos traps (SIGTRAP). getDimensionInfo is widely called — latent crash if any caller passes an unknown dim. Matches the port's force-unwrap-SIGTRAP pattern.

summary: keyedColumns dimension order is taken from an unordered Swift Dictionary instead of JS object insertion order, so detected dimension ordering can diverge from upstream.
evidence: Confirmed: keyedColumns dimensions collected via `for key in util.keys(dataDict)` over a Swift Dictionary (unordered), vs upstream `each(data)` in JS object insertion order. When keyedColumns data has no explicit `dimensions`/`encode`, the detected dimension order drives default dim->axis mapping, so ordering can diverge (and be nondeterministic across runs). Genuine divergence; mitigated in practice by name-based encode usage.

summary: buildHierarchy force-casts `children[i] as! TreeNodeOption` on dynamic user data — a non-dict child element traps at runtime instead of JS's lenient handling.
evidence: TreeNodeOption = [String:Any] (Tree.swift:52). buildHierarchy iterates `children as? [Any]` then force-casts each element `as! TreeNodeOption`. A non-dict child element (e.g. user passes children:[1,"x"]) traps at runtime, whereas upstream JS degrades it to a nameless/valueless leaf. Live path: createTree feeds tree/treemap/sunburst initData. Real crash-vs-lenience divergence, but only on atypical malformed data.

summary: color read as `styleDict?[drawType] as? ZRColor`; if the visual stores a raw color String (as the comment warns) the cast fails and params.color is silently nil, so tooltip/label markers lose their color.
evidence: Confirmed. `styleDict?[drawType] as? ZRColor` succeeds only when fill is a ZRColor enum. The palette path stores fill as ZRColor (.color) via getColorFromPalette (palette.swift:67-69), so default-colored series work. BUT when the user sets itemStyle.color, makeStyleMapper (makeStyleMapper.swift:52-54) stores fill = model.getShallow('color') = raw String, so the cast fails and params.color is silently nil -> tooltip/label color marker loses color for explicitly-colored series; medium.

summary: `val + ''` rendered via Swift interpolation `\(val!)`, so a numeric label value 3 prints "3.0" instead of JS "3" — visible label text divergence for whole-number dimension values.
evidence: Confirmed. `return val != nil ? "\(val!)" : ""` uses Swift interpolation; numeric label values stored as Double render as '3.0' where JS `val + ''` yields '3'. This runs in the `{@dim}` template-formatter label path (retrieveRawValue returns the store's Double), so whole-number dimension values render with a spurious '.0'. User-visible label text divergence; medium.

summary: Upstream throws a catchable Error when a class is missing; Swift uses fatalError, converting a recoverable condition into a hard crash.
evidence: Confirmed 231-239: fatalError replaces upstream `throw new Error`. Reachable via Scale.getClass and ComponentModel.getClass(throwWhenNotFound=true) when a user specifies an unregistered component/scale subType. Upstream throw is typically uncaught too, but Swift fatalError is unconditionally fatal (no catch possible). Crash on misconfiguration.

summary: When the 'style' prop key holds a value that is not a TextStyleProps, it is silently discarded and replaced with an empty style instead of preserving/coercing the caller's data.
evidence: In _init, key=='style' with a value not castable to TextStyleProps is dropped -> useStyle(TextStyleProps()) empty. Found a LIVE path: GraphicView constructs ZRText(textContentOption) where textContentOption is [String:Any] and its 'style' is a raw [String:Any] option dict (GraphicView.swift 165,231,235), so graphic-component text-content style (fill/font/text) is silently discarded. Typed callers (createTextStyle -> TextStyleProps, e.g. legend/visualMap/calendar/axisPointer label.style:TextStyleProps) hit the success branch and are fine. Same dict-drop also exists in Displayable.attrKV (453-457). Real feature-silently-ignored for graphic text with dict styles; niche component. Confirmed medium.

summary: JS `!!this.get('realtimeSort')` modeled as `as? Bool ?? false`, so a non-Bool but truthy realtimeSort value silently reads as false (createInvertedIndices dropped).
evidence: Confirmed as a real but low-severity risk. `(get('realtimeSort') as? Bool) ?? false` reads a non-Bool-but-truthy value (e.g. a string) as false, dropping createInvertedIndices. realtimeSort defaults to Bool false and is documented Boolean, so this only bites invalid user input. Low.

summary: Value-semantics divergence: index-prepended data is written back to self.option["data"] (upstream keeps a dual alias), so a later mergeOption that does not replace `data` would double-prepend the base-category index.

summary: Force-cast data.getItemLayout(newIdx) as! CandlestickItemLayout crashes if the layout is nil or a different type.

summary: edgeData.graph? and getEdgeByIndex are Optional but upstream assumes non-null; a nil graph/edge silently `return`s (no ribbon) instead of upstream's crash, masking a data-wiring bug.

Masks a data-wiring bug by silently drawing no ribbon. Only fires on genuine nil (error path that shouldn't occur in normal chord rendering); low.

summary: data.hostModel force-cast `as! ChordSeriesModel` will crash if hostModel is nil or a different model type.

Demoted to low: defensive-only, no live crash.

summary: renderItem `context` is a fresh [:] per datum instead of one shared object across the render round, so a user stashing cross-datum state in context loses it.

summary: data.mapDimension(...)! force-unwrapped; a latent crash if a base/value dimension is absent.
evidence: Lines 82-83,95-96 force-unwrap data.mapDimension(...)!. Latent crash if a base/value/radius/angle dim is absent; in practice always present for these series. Low.

summary: jsNumberToString is not a full ECMAScript Number->String (no exponent form); label text diverges from JS for very large/small values (>=1e15 uses Swift String(Double)).

summary: getGraph() force-unwraps getData().graph! (latent SIGTRAP if a graph series' data has no graph); comment's premise that SeriesData.graph is AnyObject? is also stale (it is typed Graph?).

Only matters when circular is force-init with fixed nodes; forceLayout iteration is DEFERRED (GraphView) -> low.

summary: mapDimension('x'/'y'/'value') is force-unwrapped; a heatmap configured without one of these dims traps at runtime instead of degrading.
evidence: mapDimension('x'/'y'/'value') force-unwrapped at L365-367; a heatmap misconfigured without one of these dims traps instead of degrading. Edge case — a valid heatmap always has these dims.

summary: Cartesian2D.getArea returns concrete Cartesian2DArea (not the protocol's CoordinateSystemClipArea?), so it fails to witness the protocol requirement and createCoordSysClipAreaSimply protocol-dispatches to the nil default — symbol clipping for scatter/line silently disabled on cartesian2d.

(default nil, CoordinateSystem.swift:319) while Cartesian2D.getArea returns concrete Cartesian2DArea (:276), so the protocol dispatch yields nil. summary: data.mapDimension(...) is force-unwrapped for base/value dims; a missing dimension would crash (latent SIGTRAP) rather than degrade.

summary: Where upstream returns undefined for a coords-only item value, the port returns NaN; downstream null/undefined checks see a number instead.

summary: For an existing region data item, upstream merges GeoJSON properties.echartsStyle into the raw item object in place; the port reads a value copy and never writes it back, so echartsStyle is dropped for regions already in series data.

Only when a GeoJSON region carries properties.echartsStyle AND the series data already has that region -> rare, low.

summary: aspectScale's upstream null value is modeled as NSNull() to retain the key; callers doing get("aspectScale") receive NSNull rather than nil, a JS-null vs NSNull vs nil divergence to audit.

The real reader geoCreator.swift:295 uses asNumberOpt(model.get('aspectScale')) which returns nil for NSNull (falls through to nil), so GEO_DEFAULT_PARAMS default applies correctly. The NSNull-vs-nil divergence is handled at the one live read site -> effectively no behavioral difference, low.

summary: data.mapDimension(dim)! force-unwrapped; a nil dimension mapping would crash instead of degrading.
evidence: data.mapDimension(dim)! force-unwrap in getTooltipPosition. Radar indicator dims are generated in getInitialData so nil is not expected in practice; latent crash risk only. Low.

summary: `data.mapDimension(axes[axisIndex].dim)!` is force-unwrapped on the assumption the indicator dim is always present; a missing/renamed indicator dim yields nil and crashes.

Byte-faithful to upstream, which also does not guard. The nil trigger (missing/renamed indicator dim) cannot occur in normal rendering; JS would pass undefined instead of crashing, so a real but dormant Swift-vs-JS SIGTRAP edge. Demoted to low severity: defensive-only, never fires on a live path.

summary: getGraph() force-unwraps getData().graph! which crashes if nil, whereas upstream returns possibly-undefined graph; also the stated type premise (AnyObject?) is stale — SeriesData.graph is now typed Graph?.
evidence: Confirmed both parts: SeriesData.graph is typed Graph? (SeriesData.swift:178) not AnyObject?, so the comment premise is stale; and getGraph() force-unwraps graph!. On the live sankey path createGraphFromNodeEdge always sets graph, so the crash is latent-only (getGraph on empty/uninitialized data).

summary: data.mapDimension(baseAxis.dim)! and valueAxis force-unwraps will fatalError if a scatter series lacks the base/value dimension.
evidence: Confirmed: data.mapDimension(baseAxis.dim)! and mapDimension(valueAxis.dim)! are force-unwrapped (lines 85-86); nil would fatalError. In practice a cartesian scatter always has both dims (same invariant LineView relies on), so crash is only on malformed series. Low likelihood.

summary: node.getModel() is Model? (nil for dataIndex<0 virtualRoot) where upstream assumes non-null; Swift guards and returns early (no sector), a null-vs-nil divergence that suppresses drawing for such nodes.
evidence: TreeNode.getModel() returns nil for dataIndex<0 (Tree.swift:271). updateData guards and returns early (no sector) where upstream (non-null model) would proceed. Affects only nodes with dataIndex<0 — chiefly the roll-up virtualRoot; its center sector may not draw when drilled in. Edge case.

summary: _updateLabel's node.getModel() is Model? (nil for virtualRoot); Swift guards and returns (no label) where upstream assumes non-null — null-vs-nil divergence.
evidence: Same null-vs-nil divergence as L126 in _updateLabel: getModel() nil for dataIndex<0 → early return (no label). Only affects virtualRoot/removed nodes. Edge case.

summary: defaultOption 'center' uses NSNull() where upstream is null; NSNull retains the key in the [String: Any] bag (vs JS null which is present too, but downstream jsTruthy/nil checks must treat NSNull as absent) — key-retention divergence to audit.
evidence: defaultOption 'center':NSNull() vs upstream null. Grep found NO tree-side reader of 'center' (only View.swift roam input, which stays nil/deferred), so no live divergence today; risk is latent for when roam lands and a jsTruthy/nil check must treat NSNull as absent. Audit item, currently harmless.

summary: node.getModel() is Optional and travelTree bails (returns) when nil, whereas upstream assumes non-null; a nil model early-returns and skips the whole subtree's visual encoding rather than processing it.
evidence: travelTree guard 'guard let nodeModel = node.getModel() else { return }' (L110) early-returns the WHOLE subtree when getModel() is nil (dataIndex<0), whereas upstream assumes non-null. Real divergence but treemap nodes are data-backed so getModel() is non-nil in practice; defensive edge case.

summary: seriesModel.designatedVisualItemStyle is a Swift value-type [String: Any]; upstream keeps it as a live-shared object read back through designatedVisualModel's parent chain, so the write→read parent-designated-visual priority may not resolve as upstream (value-copy vs reference).
evidence: Refuted as behaviorally inert. designatedVisualItemStyle is written then immediately nil'd (L198/L202); the read-back path (designatedVisualModel parent chain injected via SeriesData.wrapMethod) is a documented NO-OP (TreemapSeries.swift:165 'the injected closure is NOT actually invoked'). Parent-designated priority is instead threaded EXPLICITLY via the designatedVisual param (travelTree->mapVisual->childVisual), so the value-copy-vs-reference distinction never manifests.

summary: Upstream only defaults z/z2/cursor when el[prop] is null; the port sets the default unconditionally when the option omits the prop, so a reused (merged) element's existing z/z2/cursor is silently reset to default.

On a merge re-render where a prior option set a custom z2/z/cursor and the new option omits it, the port resets to default while upstream keeps the existing value. Edge case (merge dropping a previously-set prop); fresh elements match either way.

summary: self.ecModel! force-unwrap in optionUpdated mirrors upstream non-null assumption; crashes if component not yet mounted.
evidence: self.ecModel! force-unwrap in optionUpdated (l.200). Mirrors upstream non-null assumption; optionUpdated runs after component mount so ecModel is set in normal flow. Real crash only on out-of-order/standalone invocation. Low.

summary: legendData[i].get("name") as? String ?? "" silently coerces a numeric legend name to empty string, breaking single-select isSelected/select for number names.
evidence: legendData[i].get('name') as? String ?? '' (l.212) and the l.223 fallback coerce a numeric legend name to '' -> isSelected/select operate on the wrong key, breaking single-select init for numeric names. Real but edge: legend names are overwhelmingly strings (series names). Low.

summary: Legend item `name` is String? so numeric names coerce to nil, routing them to the pie/funnel data branch and never matching a series by a numeric name; possible latent divergence from upstream's number|string names.
evidence: Confirmed: line 252 `get('name') as? String` yields nil for numeric names; nil name -> seriesModel nil -> pie/funnel else-branch (line 327). Upstream names are number|string. Real latent divergence, but legend names are almost always series-name strings; numeric data names in pie are an edge case. Low.

summary: JS isNaN/isFinite string coercion dropped: isInfinity only examines Double values, so a string coord that JS would coerce is treated as non-infinite (guarded to the numeric ±Infinity default path).
evidence: isInfinity only inspects Double; JS isNaN/isFinite string coercion dropped. But the only inputs reaching it are the ±Double.infinity defaults assigned in markAreaTransform (L125-129) or numeric coords; a string that JS would treat as infinite is not a realistic markArea coord. Correct on the numeric path.

summary: Upstream's `|| {}` fallback dropped; getDimensionInfo returns a non-optional and can crash if the mapped dim info is genuinely absent (relies on md always resolving for markLine).
evidence: PLAUSIBLE but low. SeriesData.getDimensionInfo force-unwraps (SeriesData.swift:480 `!`). The md==nil case is guarded (else branch builds an empty SeriesDimensionDefine), so the only crash path is mapDimension returning a NON-nil dim name absent from _dimInfos — which doesn't happen in practice because mapDimension resolves through _dimInfos-derived summaries. Latent, unlikely to trigger.

summary: JS Number.prototype.toFixed rounds half-away-from-zero, but the port approximates it via String(format:'%.*f') which rounds half-to-even, so marker statistic labels on exact .5 boundaries can round differently than ECharts.
evidence: Confirmed toFixedNumber (lines 127-133) uses String(format:"%.*f") which rounds half-to-even, vs JS toFixed half-away-from-zero. Real deviation but rare: requires the marker statistic coordinate to be an exact .5 at the precision boundary (FP rarely produces exact halves), and it affects the rounded position coordinate (coordArr), off by 1 ULP in the last decimal. Cosmetic/edge — low.

summary: A visual-style color stored as ZRenderKit.ZRColor (e.g. gradient) is not matched by convertToColorStringLoose and falls through to 'transparent', collapsing the tooltip color swatch.

summary: Force-unwrap of getDataDimensionIndex(data) (base returns DimensionIndex?) 'because upstream treats it as always-present' — a nil dimension index would crash with SIGTRAP instead of the JS pass-through.
